cards.text: This is a Maskil of Asaph, one of Israel's psalm writers, and something terrible has happened to God's people. Asaph skips the "How's Your week going?" and talks straight to God. His very first line: “Why have You rejected us forever, O God?”

cards.question: Asaph asks why God's anger smolders against His people. What does Asaph call them?

cards.text: Then Asaph asks God to remember His congregation. These are the people God purchased long ago and redeemed as the tribe of His inheritance.

cards.question: Asaph reminds God of Mount ___, the place where He dwells.

cards.text: Now Asaph asks God to turn His steps to the everlasting ruins. It's like walking somebody through your place after a break-in, except this is God's own sanctuary.

cards.question: Asaph says the enemy damaged only a few things in God's sanctuary.

cards.text: Asaph tells God what happened in there. God's foes ROARED inside His meeting place and unfurled their banners as signs.

Asaph says they're like men wielding axes in a thicket of trees, smashing all the carvings with hatchets and picks. Friend, my edges wore down slowly over years of baking, and I thought I had it rough.

cards.question: Asaph pictures the foes in God's meeting place like men swinging axes through a thicket of trees. What does that picture show about them?

answers.text: They chop and smash everything in sight
They work slowly and with great care
They clear space to build something new

cards.question: After smashing the carvings, what do the enemies do to the sanctuary itself?

cards.text: Asaph even tells God what the enemies were thinking. They said in their hearts, “We will crush them completely.”

cards.question: The enemy stopped at the sanctuary and left every other place where God met His people standing.
With the meeting places burned, Asaph says there are no signs left for God's people to see. Who else is gone?

cards.text: And none of them knows how long this will last. That's being on hold with NO voice telling you how many callers are ahead of you, just the music, on repeat.

cards.question: Asaph cries out to God, asking how long the enemy will ___ Him.
Asaph says the foe's insults are aimed at God's own name.

cards.text: Then Asaph asks why God withdraws His strong right hand. He doesn't want a pep talk from God, he wants that hand.

cards.question: What does Asaph ask God to do with His strong right hand?

answers.text: Stretch it out to destroy the enemy
Raise it up to bless the land

cards.text: Then, right in the middle of all those hard questions, the psalm turns on one little word: Yet. Three letters that change EVERYTHING.

cards.question: After everything he's seen, Asaph still calls God his King from ancient times.

cards.text: Asaph starts listing what this King has done. God divided the sea by His strength and smashed the heads of the dragons of the sea.

cards.question: Asaph says God smashed the heads of the dragons of the sea. Then he names one more creature whose heads God crushed. Which one?

cards.text: God fed Leviathan to the creatures of the desert. I got replaced by a shiny new stamper and thought I had a bad day, but Leviathan had a BAD day.
Then Asaph turns to the water. God broke open the fountain and the flood.

cards.question: Asaph says God dried up rivers that were ever-flowing.

cards.text: Then Asaph looks up: “The day is Yours, and also the night; You established the moon and the sun.” Day shift and night shift, both His.

cards.question: Asaph says God set all the boundaries of the earth, and He made the ___ and the ___.

cards.text: Then Asaph goes back to asking. Remember, he tells the LORD, how the enemy has mocked You.

cards.question: Asaph says a foolish people has ___ God's name.

cards.text: Then comes a tender picture: Asaph begs God not to deliver the soul of His dove to beasts. Friend, my Minty is a dove, so this one gets me right in the apron.

cards.question: Right after pleading for God's dove, Asaph asks God not to forget the lives of someone forever. Who?
Next, Asaph points God right back to something God made with His people and asks Him to consider it. What is it?
Why does Asaph ask God to consider His covenant?

answers.text: Violence fills the dark places of the land
The people have forgotten the covenant
The enemy has written a new law

cards.text: Then Asaph prays for the people at the bottom of the pile: the oppressed, the poor and the needy.

cards.question: Asaph prays the oppressed won't retreat in shame, and that the poor and needy will ___ God's name.

cards.text: Near the end, Asaph calls on God to rise up. He asks God to remember how the fool mocks Him all day long.

cards.question: Near the end, Asaph calls on God to rise up. He says the cause he wants defended belongs to Israel alone, not to God.
Asaph has been asking God to remember the mocking. In the psalm's last line, he asks God not to disregard something. What?

findings.problem: Card 8 already tells verses 5-6 in full: the foes are 'smashing all the carvings with hatchets and picks.' Card 9 then asks what the axe picture shows, and the right answer is 'They chop and smash everything in sight.' The story card right before it gives the answer away. The right answer's 'everything in sight' also goes past the text, which says 'all the carvings.'

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Verse 7 also says the enemies 'have defiled the dwelling place of Your Name.' No card tells this. Only the burning is covered (card 10). The defiling is an important part of what Asaph lays out before God, so the baker misses it.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: 'He doesn't want a pep talk from God, he wants that hand' states what Asaph does and doesn't want as fact. The text never mentions a pep talk. The guess isn't marked as Papa Dorin's own.

rule.text: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: The turn at verse 12 is the heart of the psalm, but no card tells its second half: God is 'working salvation on the earth.' Card 1 tells only the word 'Yet,' and card 2 asks only about 'King from ancient times.' The baker misses what the King is doing.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: 'After everything he's seen' says Asaph saw the destruction himself. The psalm describes the ruins but never says the writer was there to see them. This adds a detail the text leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: 'Then he names one more creature whose heads God crushed' presents Leviathan as a different creature from the dragons of the sea in verse 13. The text sets the two lines side by side and doesn't say whether they are the same creature or different ones.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The two-blank card 'He made the ___ and the ___' needs 'summer' in blank 1 and 'winter' in blank 2. The baker can reason out that the answer is the seasons pair, but no reasoning can tell them the order. A baker who picks winter then summer gets marked wrong for not knowing the wording.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
